Rashi on Eruvin 77a:10:1.hebrew: אימא לא - משתרי, דלדידיה נמי תשמישו בקשה הוא:
Rashi on Eruvin 77a:10:1.english: Say [it is] not - Permitted, since for him, too, its use is with difficulty.

Rashi on Eruvin 77a:11:1.english: Its use does not cause worry - Whatever one places in it is protected.

Rashi on Eruvin 77a:11:2.english: Its use causes worry - For the objects fall.

Rashi on Eruvin 77a:12:1.hebrew: בא למעט - אכותל קאי, וקס"ד שעשה תל עפר למטה בקרקע סמוך לכותל, או בנה איצטבא, או הניח שם פספסים:
Rashi on Eruvin 77a:12:1.english: [If] one comes to diminish - [This] refers to a wall; and it enters your mind [to think] that he made a mound of earth below on the ground adjacent to the wall, or built a platform, or placed stones there:

Rashi on Eruvin 77a:12:2.hebrew: אם יש במעוטו ד' - אורך בצד משך הכותל, הוי כפתח. וכיון דממנו ולמעלה לא גבוה עשרה, משתמש בכל הכותל, שהרי תשמישו בנחת, שעולה לו דרך פתחו:
Rashi on Eruvin 77a:12:2.english: If its diminished [section] has four [handbreadths] - [In] length along the span of the wall, it is like an entrance. And since from it and above [the wall] is not ten [handbreadths] high, one may use the entire wall, for its use is convenient, as one ascends to it by way of its entrance.

Rashi on Eruvin 77a:13:1.hebrew: אי אהני מעוטא - למיהוי פתחא, כוליה שרי:
Rashi on Eruvin 77a:13:1.english: If the diminishing was effective - To be [considered] an opening, the entire [wall should be] permitted.

Rashi on Eruvin 77a:13:2.english: And if it was not effective - Behold, it is nullified to it [the wall].

Rashi on Eruvin 77a:13:3.hebrew: אמר רבינא - לאו מלמטה עסקינן, דהתם ודאי בציר מד' לא מהני למידי. אלא כגון שעקר חוליא מראשו — מגובהו של כותל קרי "ראשו", כדתנן: "היו בראשו פירות". הלכך, אי הוי מעוטא ארבעה אורך — הוי פיתחא לכל הכותל; בציר מהכא — פיתחא הוא דלא הוי, אבל לאשתמושי ביה שרי, דכיון דלא גבוה י', לא הוי רשותא:
Rashi on Eruvin 77a:13:3.english: Ravina said: We are not dealing with [diminishing the wall] from below, for there, certainly, less than four [handbreadths] accomplishes nothing. Rather, [it is a case] such as where one removed a segment [of stone] from its top — [the Gemara] calls the height of the wall "its top," as we learned in a mishnah: "If there were fruits on its top." Therefore, if the diminished section was four [handbreadths] in length, it is [considered] an entrance for the entire wall; [if it was] less than this, it is [only] that it does not constitute an entrance, but to make use of it is permitted, for since it is not ten [handbreadths] high, it does not constitute a [separate] domain.

Rashi on Eruvin 77a:14:1.hebrew: כפה ספל - סמוך לכותל, ומיעט גובהו מעשרה. כל הני מיעוטי — כגון דליכא י' מראשו לראש הכותל:
Rashi on Eruvin 77a:14:1.english: [If] one overturned a basin - [He placed it] adjacent to the wall, and diminished its height [to less] than ten [handbreadths]. All these [cases of] diminishing [refer to a case] such as where there are not ten [handbreadths] from its top to the top of the wall.

Rashi on Eruvin 77a:16:1.english: What of it? - It is still [an item that may be] moved on Shabbat.

Rashi on Eruvin 77a:16:2.hebrew: פגה - תאנה בוסר, שטומנין אותה בתבן להתבשל. ותבן מוקצה הוא ואסור לטלטלו, כגון שהקצהו ללבון לבנים:
Rashi on Eruvin 77a:16:2.english: An unripe fig - An unripe fig, which one buries in straw to ripen. And straw is muktzeh and forbidden to move, such as where one set it aside for making bricks.

Rashi on Eruvin 77a:16:3.hebrew: וחררה שהטמינה - אתמול בגחלים, ועכשיו כבו, ומ"מ מוקצין הן. אבל לא כבו — לא, דמתוך שנהפכים, מכבה את התחתונות ומבעיר את העליונות, כדאמרינן בכריתות (דף כ.):
Rashi on Eruvin 77a:16:3.english: And a cake that one buried - [He buried it] yesterday in coals, and now they were extinguished; and nevertheless, they are set aside [muktzeh]. But [if] they were not extinguished, no, [it may not be taken], for as they turn over, he extinguishes the lower ones and kindles the upper ones, as we say in Keritot (20a).

Rashi on Eruvin 77a:17:1.hebrew: דאית להו אוגניים - כעין ספלים שלנו, דעכשיו עפר מונח עליהן, והוי מזיז עפר ממקומו ודומה לחופר:
Rashi on Eruvin 77a:17:1.english: That they have rims - Like our basins, so that now earth rests upon them, and he moves earth from its place and it is similar to digging.

Rashi on Eruvin 77a:18:1.english: One who buries - To store [them] away:

Rashi on Eruvin 77a:1:1.hebrew: מעלין - מחצירן לראשו, והוא הדין דמורידין, דמקום פטור הוא, ובטיל לכאן ולכאן להקל:
Rashi on Eruvin 77a:1:1.english: May raise - From their courtyard to its top. And the same applies to lowering [food], for it is an exempt domain and is nullified to this side and to that side to be lenient.

Rashi on Eruvin 77a:4:1.hebrew: מקום שאין בו ד' - רוחב, ועומד בין רה"י לרה"ר, ויש לנו היכר, כגון גבוה מן הארץ ג'. ואילו היה רוחב ד', היה נקרא רשות לעצמו והויא כרמלית, ואסור לכאן ולכאן. אבל עכשיו, נקרא מקום פטור, ומותר לכאן ולכאן לכתף עליו משאוי שלהן:
Rashi on Eruvin 77a:4:1.english: A place that does not have four [handbreadths] - [In] width, and it stands between a private domain and a public domain, and we have a recognizable distinction, such as [its being] three [handbreadths] high above the ground. For had it been four [handbreadths in] width, it would have been called an independent domain and would be a karmelit, and [transferring objects] would be forbidden both to this [side] and to that [side]. But now, it is called an exempt domain, and it is permitted both to this [side] and to that [side] to adjust their burden upon it.

Rashi on Eruvin 77a:4:2.hebrew: ובלבד שלא יחליפו - דרבנן היא, דאילו חיובא ליכא, דבעינן עקירה מרשות זו והנחה לרשות זו, והכא עקירה מרה"י גמורה והנחה למקום פטור, ועקירה ממקום פטור והנחה לרה"ר גמורה:
Rashi on Eruvin 77a:4:2.english: Provided they do not exchange - [This prohibition] is rabbinic, for there is no [Torah] liability, as we require uprooting from this domain and depositing into that domain [for one to be liable], whereas here, [there is] uprooting from a full private domain and depositing into an exempt domain, and uprooting from an exempt domain and depositing into a full public domain.

Rashi on Eruvin 77a:5:1.hebrew: ורב לית ליה דרב דימי - בתמיה: והא מתניתא היא במסכת שבת בפ"ק [דף ו.]: עומד אדם על האסקופה, נוטל מעני ונותן לו, מבעל הבית ונותן לו, ובלבד שלא יטול מזה ויתן לזה:
Rashi on Eruvin 77a:5:1.english: And does Rav not accept [the ruling] of Rav Dimi? - [This is asked] in astonishment: But is this not a baraita in Tractate Shabbat, in the first chapter [daf 6a]: "A person may stand on the threshold, take from a poor person and give to him, [or take] from a homeowner and give to him, provided that he does not take from this [one] and give to that [one]"?

Rashi on Eruvin 77a:5:2.english: Domains by Torah law - Such as a public domain and a private domain.

Rashi on Eruvin 77a:6:1.hebrew: דרבנן - חצירות, דרשות יחיד ויחיד הוא, ומדרבנן הוא דאסור:
Rashi on Eruvin 77a:6:1.english: By rabbinic law - Courtyards, for they are [each] a private domain and a private domain, and it is [only] by rabbinic law that [carrying between them] is prohibited:

Rashi on Eruvin 77a:7:1.hebrew: וצידו אחד שוה לארץ - כלומר, גבוה הוא מן האחת ונמוך הוא לחברתה, כגון שקרקעיתה של זו גבוה. כל כמה דלא גבוה י', קרי ליה שוה לארץ:
Rashi on Eruvin 77a:7:1.english: And its other side is level with the ground - That is to say, it is high from [the side of] one [courtyard] and low to its fellow, such as where the ground of this [latter one] is elevated. As long as it is not ten [handbreadths] high, [he] calls it “level with the ground.”

Rashi on Eruvin 77a:7:2.hebrew: נותנין אותו - להעלות ולהוריד מעליו, וחבירו אסור:
Rashi on Eruvin 77a:7:2.english: They grant it - To bring [objects] up and bring [them] down from it, while his neighbor is forbidden.

Rashi on Eruvin 77a:9:1.hebrew: חריץ - על פני אורך החצירות, מבדיל בין זו לזו — הוי מחיצה מעלייתא:
Rashi on Eruvin 77a:9:1.english: A ditch - [Running] along the length of the courtyards, separating between this [one] and that [one], it constitutes a proper partition.

Rashi on Eruvin 77a:9:2.hebrew: שוה לארץ - שאינו עמוק ממנה י', כגון שקרקעיתה נמוך:
Rashi on Eruvin 77a:9:2.english: Level with the ground - That it is not ten [handbreadths] deep from it, for example, where its ground is low.

Tosafot on Eruvin 77a:18:1.hebrew: הטומן לפת וצנון כו' - בשלא השרישו איירי, דכשהשרישו לא היו ניטלין בשבת. וא"ת: בשלמא גבי כלאים ושביעית אצטריך לאשמועי' דלא גזרינן כשמתכוון להטמין אמו דילמא אתי ליטע; אבל מעשר מה שייך כאן? אפי' השריש, כיון דליכא תוספת! ואי נקטינן לענין דשרי לעשר עליו מן התלוש או ממנו על התלוש, ולא חיישינן דילמא אתי לפרושי מן התלוש על המחובר ומן המחובר על התלוש — א"כ הוה ליה למנקט תרומה, דגבי מחובר ותלוש רגיל להזכיר תרומה בכל מקום: "אין תורמין מן התלוש על המחובר", "פירות ערוגה זו תלושין יהיו תרומה על פירות מחוברין". ואור"י: דרגילות הוא שמתוספין מחמת ליחלוחית הקרקע, כעין שאנו רואין שומין ובצלים שמתוספין אפילו כשמונחים בחלון; ועל אותה תוספת קאמר דאין צריך לעשר, הואיל והיו מתוקנים מקודם לכן. ודוקא נקט "הטומן", אבל אם לשם נטיעה עושה — חושש משום כולם:
Tosafot on Eruvin 77a:18:1.english: "One who buries a turnip or a radish, etc." - It is dealing with [a case] where they did not take root, for had they taken root, they would not be [permitted to be] taken [from the ground] on Shabbat. And if you say: Granted regarding kilayim and the Sabbatical Year, it was necessary to teach us that we do not decree [a prohibition] when one intends to bury [produce], lest he come to plant; but regarding tithe, how does it apply here? Even if it took root, since there is no additional growth! And if we take [the ruling] to mean that it is permitted to tithe for it from detached [produce] or from it for detached [produce], and we are not concerned lest one come to separate [tithes] from detached [produce] for attached [produce] or from attached [produce] for detached [produce] — if so, [the mishna] should have mentioned terumah, for regarding attached and detached [produce], [the Tanna] is accustomed everywhere to mention terumah: "One may not separate terumah from detached [produce] for attached [produce]," "[May] the detached fruits of this bed be terumah for attached fruits"! And the Ri explains: It is common that they grow additionally due to the moisture of the soil, similar to what we see with garlic and onions, which grow additionally even when placed in a window; and regarding that additional growth, [the mishna] says that one does not need to tithe [it], since they were already rectified prior to that. And specifically [the mishna] formulated: "One who buries"; but if he acts for the sake of planting, he must be concerned on account of all of them.

Tosafot on Eruvin 77a:1:1.hebrew: ורבי יוחנן אמר אלו מעלין כו' - פירוש: מן הבית; דמן החצר — אפילו ברחב ד' שרי, דכר"ש מוקי לה רבי יוחנן לקמן בריש כל גגות (עירובין דף צב.):
Tosafot on Eruvin 77a:1:1.english: "And Rabbi Yoḥanan said: These may raise, etc." - Explanation: [Rabbi Yoḥanan means raising food] from the house; for from the courtyard, even [if the wall is] four [handbreadths] wide, it is permitted, as Rabbi Yoḥanan establishes it in accordance with Rabbi Shimon later, at the beginning of [the chapter] Kol Gagot (Eruvin 92a).

Tosafot on Eruvin 77a:3:1.hebrew: עולין אין מעלין לא - תימה: דמאי קס"ד? וכי לא ידע דרבי יוחנן איירי באין לו ארבעה? וי"ל: דס"ד דטעמא דרבי יוחנן משום דאין רגילות להשתמש שם, ולא אסרי אהדדי, והוא הדין ברוחב ד' — כיון שהוא גבוה י' ואין נח להשתמש שם. ולהכי לא פריך אלא לר' יוחנן; אבל לרב, דטעמא משום דבטל הוא, לא שייך אלא באין בו ד' על ד':
Tosafot on Eruvin 77a:3:1.english: "To ascend, yes; to raise, no" - [This is] astonishing: For what did [the Gemara] think initially? Did it not know that Rabbi Yoḥanan is speaking of [a wall] that does not have [a width of] four [handbreadths]? And it can be answered: [The Gemara] initially assumed that Rabbi Yoḥanan's reasoning is that it is not customary to use [the top of the wall], and [therefore the two courtyards] do not prohibit each other; and the same [logic would] apply to [a wall with a] width of four [handbreadths], since it is ten [handbreadths] high and it is not convenient to use [it] there. And for this reason [the Gemara] raised a difficulty only against Rabbi Yoḥanan; but according to Rav, whose reasoning is that [the wall's surface] is nullified [to the courtyards], that applies only where it does not have four by four [handbreadths].

Tosafot on Eruvin 77a:6:1.hebrew: הכא במאי עסקינן ברשויות דרבנן - נראה דוקא כי הכא, שהכל רה"י אלא שלא עירבו; אבל מקום שאין בו ד' על ד' שבין רה"י לכרמלית — אין נראה שיחלוק רב, אלא מותר לבני רה"י ולבני כרמלית לכתף עליו. וקצת מוכח כן בפ"ק (דף ט.), דמוקי רבא הא דאמר רב: "תוך הפתח, אע"פ שאין בו ד' על ד', צריך לחי, אמר, להתירו" — הפתוח לכרמלית, משום דמצא מין את מינו; ולרה"ר שרי, ולא קאמר משום דעשו חיזוק. אלא ודאי, אף לרב, בין כרמלית לרה"י לא עשו חיזוק. ומיהו מצינו למימר, דהתם לא נקט טעמא דחיזוק משום דאית ליה טעמא אחרינא:
Tosafot on Eruvin 77a:6:1.english: "With what are we dealing here? With domains by rabbinic law" - It appears [that this applies] specifically like here, where everything is a private domain, except that they did not merge [via an eruv]; but regarding a place that does not have [an area of] four by four [handbreadths] that is between a private domain and a karmelit, it does not appear that Rav would disagree; rather, it is permitted for the people of the private domain and the people of the karmelit to adjust burdens upon it. And this is somewhat proven in the first chapter (9a), where Rava establishes that which Rav said, "The space within the entranceway, even though it does not have [an area of] four by four [handbreadths], requires a side post, he said, to permit it," [as referring to an entranceway] that opens to a karmelit, because "it found its own kind and was awakened"; whereas [if it opens] to a public domain, it is permitted, and [the Gemara] did not say [that it requires a side post] because they reinforced [their words]. Rather, certainly, even according to Rav, between a karmelit and a private domain they did not reinforce [their words]. However, we could say that there, [the Gemara] did not cite the reason of reinforcement because it has another reason.

Tosafot on Eruvin 77a:6:2.hebrew: ברשויות דרבנן - בפרק כיצד משתתפין מיקל רב דימי טפי משמיה דרבי יוחנן ברשויות דרבנן, ושרי אחילו להחליף כשיש בין רשות היחיד לכרמלית מקום שאין בו ד' על ד'. והא דאמר ר' יוחנן הכא: "אלו מעלין מכאן ואוכלין" — מסיק דזעירי אמרה:
Tosafot on Eruvin 77a:6:2.english: With domains by rabbinic law - In the chapter [entitled] "Keitzad Mishtatfin," Rav Dimi is even more lenient in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan regarding rabbinic domains, and permits even exchanging [objects between them] when there is a place that is not four by four [handbreadths] between a private domain and a karmelit. And as for that which Rabbi Yoḥanan said here, "These may raise [food] from here and eat" — [the Gemara later] concludes that Ze'iri said it.

Tosafot on Eruvin 77a:7:1.hebrew: כותל שבין ב' חצירות גבוה עשרה וצדו אחד שוה לארץ - לאו שוה ממש קאמר, דאם כן לאו היינו כותל, אלא הכל היא קרקעית חצר; אלא כל שאין גבוה י' — "שוה לארץ" קרי ליה. כך פי' בקונטרס. וא"ת: לרב חסדא, דאמר בפרק כל גגות (לקמן עירובין דף צג:) "גידוד ה' ומחיצה ה' אין מצטרפין" — מאי קאמר "נותנין אותו לזה ששוה לארץ"? הא אין מטלטלין בעליונה אלא בד'! וי"ל: דמכל מקום נפקא מינה, דתוך ד' מיהא שרי לטלטל מן הכותל לעליונה:
Tosafot on Eruvin 77a:7:1.english: A wall that is between two courtyards, [one of its sides is] ten [handbreadths] high and its other side is level with the ground - He does not mean literally level, for if so, this would not be a wall, but rather all of it would be the ground of the courtyard; rather, whatever is not ten [handbreadths] high, he calls "level with the ground." So it was explained in the Kuntres. And if you say: According to Rav Chisda, who said in the chapter [entitled] Kol Gagot (below, Eruvin 93b), "An embankment of five [handbreadths] and a partition of five [handbreadths] do not combine," what does he mean by saying, "We assign it to the one [facing the courtyard] where it is level with the ground"? Isn't it [forbidden to] carry in the upper [courtyard] except within four [cubits]? And one can say: That nevertheless, there is a practical difference, in that within four [cubits] at least, it is permitted to carry from the wall to the upper [courtyard].
